title: How Adam Robinson bootstrapped three SaaS companies to $1M ARR, faster each time
summary: Adam walks through reaching $1M ARR with Robly (17 months), Retention.com (27 weeks) and RB2B (16 weeks). Each used a distribution channel with little competition, and RB2B was built audience-first via founder-led LinkedIn content. He is candid about the failures, high churn and layoffs behind the wins.

principles.text: Customer acquisition is expensive because of competition; find an uncontested channel with a good offer.
principles.quote: what makes acquiring customers expensive is competition and if you have a channel that you don't have any competition in and you have a good offer is going to be incredibly inexpensive for you to acquire those customers.

principles.text: Do things that don't scale early: manual onboarding to the activation moment keeps customers sticking.
principles.quote: We knew the magic moment was getting someone to hit send on their first campaign. If we could do that, they stuck 100% of the time.

principles.text: A fast-payback ad channel can still bring bad customers; for SaaS, Facebook ads often attract high-churn wannabes.
principles.quote: I think for SAS, it very rarely works to do Facebook ads because you bring in these wannabes that, you know, it's like a 15% per month churn customer

principles.text: Sell before you build; building for a launch nobody wants wastes a year.
principles.quote: how I advocate building for building companies now, like sell before you buy.

principles.text: Distribution channels decay; build for how go-to-market works now, not what worked before.
principles.quote: it's like product and distribution and what is available at the time, you know, that determines what grows, right?

principles.text: Treat yourself as being in the edutainment business; great organic social content is the most efficient trust-builder.
principles.quote: My job is to make entertaining, educational, and highly compelling content about how I am building my SAS and about how you can do it, too.
